newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak shares quiet, SAX down 0.07 pts to 195.07.
newsitem.headline: Slovak shares quiet, SAX down 0.07 pts to 195.07.

text.p: 1430 GMT - Slovak shares were mostly quiet, leaving the SAX index only 0.07 point lower in flat trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Thursday and with the bourse's turnover supported mainly by OTC deals.
*Nafta NAFT.BV did not trade, VUB Bank VSEO.BV up 30 to 1,530 crowns, VSZ unchanged at 750, Slovnaft did not trade, Biotika BIOL.BV up 48 at 898 crowns.
Slovak shares were mostly quiet in flat trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday but turnover on the bourse was high, supported mainly by some direct deals in steel maker VSZ.
The BSE posted a turnover of 457.34 million crowns, out of which more than 260 million was in VSZ shares, traded over-the-counter at 750 crowns, the same price as on the bourse floor.
"We're quite impressed by the fact that the floor price in VSZ has not been changing, even now when there is no dividend involved," Bohus Betko of ING Barings said.
Last week, the company announced it would pay a 40-crown dividend per share, double the previous year's, helping the issue to rise to 750 crowns.
"Unfortunately, nothing much interesting happened apart from VSZ," Betko said, adding that the general lack of liquidity in Bratislava might be a reason why VSZ's price has not changed.
"When you have hardly any shares that are really liquid on the bourse, you simply must accept some pain in trading with them," he added.

Overall volume increased to 940,563 shares, from 132,618 shares traded on Wednesday, while turnover climbed to 457.34 million crowns from 33.91 million. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
